scope: Machu Picchu, Peru - key structures in their current ruin state (schematic)
title: Machu Picchu
blurb: Machu Picchu as it stands today: the 15th-century Inca citadel open to the sky. The thatched roofs are gone, so the Temple of the Sun, the Temple of the Three Windows, the Main Temple, the Temple of the Condor and the residential houses survive as roofless walls shown at schematic reduced heights, while the Intihuatana, the Royal Tomb, the fountains, the agricultural terraces and the mountain setting endure much as the Incas left them. This model covers the key structures, not the whole mountain.

systems.name: Temple of the Sun
systems.description: The Intiwasi: the only Inca construction with a semicircular shape, a curved ashlar wall about 10.5 m across built on a natural granite rock, with three windows aligned to the solstices.

systems.name: Royal Tomb
systems.description: The natural cave beneath the Temple of the Sun, enhanced with carved walls, niches, an altar and a throne-like carving for the highest-ranking dead.

systems.name: Intihuatana
systems.description: The "hitching post of the sun": a ritual stone carved directly from the mountain bedrock in the upper Sacred Sector, linked to shadows, solar movement and ritual timing.

systems.name: Temple of the Three Windows
systems.description: The 10 by 8 m chamber in the Hanan sector whose three east-facing trapezoidal windows mark the winter solstice, summer solstice and equinox, and the three Inca worlds.

systems.name: Main Temple
systems.description: The Principal Temple: three walls 11 by 8 m with trapezoidal niches, its west corner collapsed by earthquake, a carved altar rock ahead of it, and a Southern Cross sculpture.

systems.name: Temple of the Condor
systems.description: The condor carved from living rock: head stone, ruff stones, outstretched wing rocks, a possible sacrificial altar, and a subterranean chamber with grottos and passageways.

systems.name: Fountains and water
systems.description: Eight of the sixteen Stairway of Fountains, gravity-fed by a spring canal about 749 m long at a 3% slope, with the royal fountain first and the private Condor fountain last.

systems.name: Agricultural terraces
systems.description: Stone retaining walls and planting platforms stepping down the west and south slopes, holding the mountain dry and stable as well as growing its crops.

systems.name: Residential sector
systems.description: Elite houses, commoner house rows and storehouses (colcas) as they stand today: open to the sky, the thatched gable roofs gone and the stone walls at schematic ruin heights; every doorway and window is trapezoidal.

systems.name: Plazas and access
systems.description: The Sacred Plaza and Central Plaza, the Main Gate, the Guardhouse, the Sun Gate (Intipunku), and the stairways that thread the single-storey city together.

systems.name: Terrain context
systems.description: The mountain saddle at 2,430 m between Machu Picchu mountain and Huayna Picchu, with the Urubamba River below. Context geometry only; counts and contours are schematic.

explanations.temple rock platform: The massive natural granite rock on which the Temple of the Sun is built, the fusion of human craftsmanship and the living earth that makes the temple exceptional. Rock massing is schematic.
explanations.bedrock core: The top of the natural rock fills most of the temple interior, carved with long flat sections for use as an altar. Exact carved sections are schematic.
explanations.sun temple altar rock: The carved altar sections on the temple rock, believed to have been used for ceremonies honoring the Sun God Inti. Exact carving is schematic.
explanations.curved wall, north arc: Part of the semicircular curved outer wall of the Temple of the Sun, finely polished ashlar fitted so precisely that not even a blade of grass can pass between the stones. The curve is unique in Machu Picchu and rare in the Inca Empire. Today the temple stands roofless; the wall is shown here at a schematic partial height, not a measured one. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.curved wall, east arc: Part of the semicircular curved outer wall of the Temple of the Sun, about 10.5 m in diameter, built of finely polished ashlar. Today the temple stands roofless; the wall is shown here at a schematic partial height, not a measured one. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.curved wall, south arc: Part of the semicircular curved outer wall of the Temple of the Sun. Today the temple stands roofless; the wall is shown here at a schematic partial height, not a measured one. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.west straight wall: The straight wall closing the D-shaped plan of the Temple of the Sun, shown at a schematic partial height. Exact length is schematic.
explanations.north window: The largest of the three Temple of the Sun windows, facing north, with a unique form cut into the stones at its base and small crafted holes in the base stones. Damage at its rear is believed to be from a lightning strike. Shown lowered into the reduced wall of the ruin state; exact opening size is schematic.
explanations.east window (winter solstice): One of two east-facing windows of the Temple of the Sun, oriented to the winter solstice sunrise on 21 June, when the sun returns. According to post-conquest chronicles, large golden discs were mounted below the windows. Shown lowered into the reduced wall of the ruin state; exact alignment and opening are schematic.
explanations.east window (summer solstice): One of two east-facing windows of the Temple of the Sun, oriented to the summer solstice sunrise on 22 December. Shown lowered into the reduced wall of the ruin state; exact alignment and opening are schematic.
explanations.sun temple niches: Worship niches in the Temple of the Sun wall, shifted down to match the reduced wall of the ruin state. Their count and placement are schematic.
explanations.sun temple foundation course: The foundation course of the curved wall, wider than the wall above. Exact foundation depth is schematic.
explanations.sun temple access stair: The stair leading up to the Temple of the Sun. Access to the temple interior is restricted today. Exact stair placement is schematic.
explanations.tomb floor: The floor of the Royal Tomb cave. Exact floor level is schematic.
explanations.tomb back wall and niches: The carved back wall of the Royal Tomb with niches for sacred bundles or offerings honoring the ancestors. Exact niche count is schematic.
explanations.tomb west wall: The carved west wall of the Royal Tomb cave. Exact carving is schematic.
explanations.tomb east wall: The carved east wall of the Royal Tomb cave. Exact carving is schematic.
explanations.tomb roof slab: The rock roof of the Royal Tomb, carrying the Temple of the Sun above. Exact thickness is schematic.
explanations.tomb altar stone: The carved altar stone in the Royal Tomb. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.tomb throne carving: The throne-like carving in the Royal Tomb. Its fine masonry suggests the tomb was intended for the highest-ranking individuals, possibly the emperor Pachacuti. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.tomb entrance lintel: The lintel over the entrance to the Royal Tomb cave. Exact opening is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana bedrock knoll: The bedrock knoll in the upper Sacred Sector from which the Intihuatana is carved. Exact knoll height is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana ritual stone: The Intihuatana, the "hitching post of the sun": a ritual stone carved directly from the mountain bedrock, commonly described as about 1.70 m high with an 8.60 m perimeter. Its carved planes and edges are linked to shadows, solar movement and ritual timing. It was damaged in 2000 during filming of a beer commercial. Exact carving is schematic.

explanations.intihuatana top platform: The platform ringing the Intihuatana stone. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana retaining wall: The retaining wall of the Intihuatana terrace. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana access stair: The stair climbing to the Intihuatana terrace. The stone can be visited only in the morning and touching is prohibited. Exact stair placement is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana lower terrace: The lower terrace below the Intihuatana. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.intihuatana perimeter niches: Niches around the Intihuatana terrace. Their count and placement are schematic.
explanations.intihuatana south outcrop: The natural rock outcrop south of the Intihuatana terrace. Exact massing is schematic.

explanations.middle trapezoidal window: The middle trapezoidal window of the Temple of the Three Windows. Exact opening is schematic.

explanations.three windows offering niches: The niches flanking the Temple of the Three Windows, where gold and silver objects were placed during ceremonies. Their fineness marks this as one of the most important ceremonial spaces in Machu Picchu. Shifted down to match the reduced walls of the ruin state; exact niche count is schematic.
explanations.main temple north wall: The north wall of the Main Temple, one of three sturdy walls of rectangular stones with precise joints, 11 m long by 8 m wide overall with walls 90 cm thick. Today the temple stands roofless; the wall is shown here at a schematic partial height, not a measured one. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.main temple central wall: The central wall of the Main Temple, carrying seven trapezoidal niches. Today the temple stands roofless; the wall is shown here at a schematic partial height, not a measured one. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.main temple south wall: The south wall of the Main Temple, shown at a schematic partial height for the ruin state. Exact coursing is schematic.
explanations.main temple collapsed west corner: The west corner of the Main Temple, displaced by seismic activity and water leaks, at risk of collapse. Modeled as fallen blocks; exact collapse pattern is schematic.
explanations.main temple niches: The trapezoidal niches of the Main Temple: seven in the central wall and five in each side wall. Exact niche shapes are schematic.
explanations.main temple altar rock: The large partially carved rock about 10 m ahead of the Main Temple, thought to have served as a sacrificial altar. Exact carving is schematic.
explanations.southern cross sculpture: The small stone sculpture depicting the Southern Cross constellation beside the Main Temple, casting a llama-head shadow at the winter solstice. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.main temple floor platform: The floor platform of the Main Temple. Holes for roof beams survive but there is no evidence the temple was ever roofed. Exact platform extent is schematic.
explanations.condor head stone: The flat triangular rock forming the condor head, with carved eyes and beak. It may have served as a sacrificial altar. Exact carving is schematic.
explanations.condor ruff stones: The abutting semicircular stones representing the condor neck ruff. Exact arrangement is schematic.
explanations.condor left wing rock: One of two outstretched rock formations shaped into the wings of a swooping condor. Exact wing geometry is schematic.
explanations.condor right wing rock: One of two outstretched rock formations shaped into the wings of a swooping condor. Exact wing geometry is schematic.
explanations.condor sacrificial altar: The stone before the condor head that may have served as a sacrificial altar. Its role is debated; exact form is schematic.
explanations.condor temple north wall: The enclosing wall of the Temple of the Condor on the north side, shown at a schematic partial height for the ruin state. Exact wall line is schematic.
